message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (dir. John Carpenter) | A tense, claustrophobic alien invasion with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (dir. Jonathan Demme) | A psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑procedural intrigue. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (dir. Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a new wave of horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | Fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | Dark, inventive, and a launchpad for a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (dir. Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage film that made a huge cultural impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A modern classic that blends supernatural scares with strong storytelling. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (dir. Drew Goddard) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and genuinely scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (dir. Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burn, atmospheric horror set in 17th‑century New England. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that’s as clever as it is terrifying. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence, with a strong family dynamic. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s unsettlingly beautiful and psychologically complex. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of a classic tale with strong feminist themes. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (dir. Nia DaCosta) | A fresh take on a horror legend with a powerful social commentary. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (dir. Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that blends creepy atmosphere with a compelling story. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (dir. Gerard Johnstone) | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s both funny and creepy. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
